title: FSMoE: A Flexible and Scalable Training System for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Models
problem: Existing MoE training systems (DeepSpeed-MoE, Tutel) support only limited routing functions and use fixed or heuristic pipeline degrees, leaving significant communication overhead because they fail to overlap inter-node AlltoAll dispatch/combine with intra-node ESP-AllGather/ESP-ReduceScatter communications, and do not co-design Gradient-AllReduce scheduling with MoE-layer communication.
motivation: AlltoAll communication in MoE layers accounts for 30-60% of total training time, and the combination of multiple parallelisms (DP+MP+EP+ESP) creates complex overlapping opportunities that existing systems miss, causing up to 50%+ communication overhead on GPU clusters.
method: FSMoE divides each mixture-of-experts layer into six customizable pieces (Gate, Order, I-Order, Dispatch, Combine, Expert) with a two-phase profiler measuring matrix operations (GEMM) and network communications. It overlaps three streams simultaneously—each node sending data to all others (AlltoAll), coordinating data within each node (ESP-AllGather/ReduceScatter), and expert computation—by identifying the bottleneck and selecting the optimal batch-size per scenario through optimization (SLSQP), while also splitting synchronization (Gradient-AllReduce) into chunks that fit idle computation gaps, refined by greedy search then evolutionary optimization.
key_novelty: FSMoE is the first mixture-of-experts system to overlap both between-node communication (AlltoAll) and within-node communication (ESP-AllGather/ReduceScatter) with expert computation by adapting batch-sizes per scenario, while also partitioning gradient synchronization (Gradient-AllReduce) work into idle pipeline gaps.
contributions: A modular MoE abstraction with six sub-modules, four pre-built gating functions, and hook-based extensibility supporting any routing mechanism.
A three-stream scheduling algorithm that overlaps intra-node and inter-node communications with computation, using SLSQP-solved optimal pipeline degrees per phase.
An adaptive gradient partitioning method that fully hides Gradient-AllReduce within overlappable compute/communication windows across MoE and dense layers.
1.18x-1.22x speedup over Tutel+PipeMoE on 1458 configured MoE layers; 1.19x-3.01x speedup over DeepSpeed-MoE on real-world GPT-2 and Mixtral models on up to 48-GPU clusters.

metrics.speedup: 1.18x-1.22x over Tutel+PipeMoE on 1458 MoE layer configs; 1.19x-3.01x over DeepSpeed-MoE on GPT-2/Mixtral real-world models
metrics.other: up to 1.42x speedup on individual gating function benchmarks vs DeepSpeed-MoE; performance model fitting r^2 >= 0.9999 for all collective types

baselines: Tutel-Improved (PipeMoE + Gradient-AllReduce overlap with dense ops)
limitations: Evaluated on clusters up to 48 GPUs with commodity RTX A6000 and RTX 2080Ti GPUs connected via InfiniBand; scaling behavior on larger production clusters (e.g., 1000+ GPUs with H100/NVLink) is not characterized.
primary_theme: Adaptive communication-computation pipeline scheduling for sparse MoE training
